title: K-flat scalar cone and its natural total-tensor model
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a closed braided monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian, def-sfb-monoidal-category, lem-sfb-derived-monoidal]. Let $B$ be a commutative ring acting linearly on $\mathcal A$, with $(b u)\otimes v=b(u\otimes v)=u\otimes(b v)$ for morphisms $u,v$ and $b\in B$. Fix $b\in B$, and put
$$P_b=\operatorname{Cone}(b:\mathbf1[0]\to\mathbf1[0]),$$
with the cochain and cone conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $P_b$ is K-flat for the total tensor product and two-sided quasi-isomorphism convention of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. For every unbounded cochain complex $C$ there is an isomorphism of complexes
$$\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes P_b)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(b:C\to C),$$
natural in chain maps $C\to C'$. If $Q$ is cochain localization, its composite with the canonical K-flat tensor comparison gives isomorphisms
$$QC\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\operatorname{Cone}(b:C\to C),$$
natural in $C$. Thus the displayed cochain cone functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms after localization and descends with these isomorphisms to a functor naturally isomorphic to $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b$ on $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: DerivedCategory.kFlat_scalarCone (lines 67-76), isIso_μ_scalarCone (79-88), tensorScalarConeIso' (103-116), tensorScalarConeIso'_hom_naturality (120-134), tensorScalarConeIso (147-149), and tensorScalarConeIso_hom_naturality (152-158); binder context at 37-42.

proof.text:
Use the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], ordering its summands as $C^n\oplus C^{n+1}$. Thus $P_b^{-1}=\mathbf1$, $P_b^0=\mathbf1$, and its only differential is $b$. Additivity makes tensoring a zero object zero, so the total tensors of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] have just two nonzero summands in each degree. Via the unitors of [def-sfb-monoidal-category], order both as $C^n\oplus C^{n+1}$. On the right tensor $T_R(C)=\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes P_b)$ the differential is
$$d_R^n(x,y)=(d_Cx+(-1)^{n+1}by,d_Cy).$$
On $T_L(C)=\operatorname{Tot}(P_b\otimes C)$ it is
$$d_L^n(x,y)=(d_Cx+by,-d_Cy).$$
These are biproduct matrix formulas, with $(x,y)$ denoting the two inclusions, not elements of an arbitrary abelian category. The $B$-linearity assumption identifies the differential contributed by $P_b$ with the displayed scalar on $C$. Put $s_n=(-1)^{n+1}$. The maps $\Phi_C^n=\operatorname{diag}(1,s_n)$ satisfy $\Phi_C^{n+1}d_R^n=d_L^n\Phi_C^n$, since $s_{n+1}=-s_n$ and $s_n^2=1$. Their inverses are the same diagonal maps. The formula for $d_L$ is exactly the cone differential, so this constructs $\Phi_C:T_R(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(b:C\to C)$ and $\Psi_C:T_L(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(b:C\to C)$.

source.place: scalarCone and tensorScalarConeIso', lines 55-57 and 102-116; degreewise sign calculation expanded using the item's cone convention

proof.text: For a chain map $f:C\to C'$, $B$-linearity gives $f\circ b_C=b_{C'}\circ f$. Define $F_b(f)=\operatorname{diag}(f^n,f^{n+1})$ between the cones. The differential matrices from [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] show this is a chain map; diagonal identities and compositions show that $F_b(C)=\operatorname{Cone}(b_C)$ is a functor. The tensor-map formula of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], together with naturality of the unitors in [def-sfb-monoidal-category], identifies both $T_R(f)$ and $T_L(f)$ with the same diagonal matrix. This commutes with $\operatorname{diag}(1,s_n)$ and with the identity. Consequently $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are natural in all chain maps, including quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: tensorScalarConeIso'_hom_naturality, lines 118-134; diagonal formula and functoriality expanded

proof.text:
For every $C$ there is a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes $0\to C\to F_b(C)\to C[1]\to0$, with maps the first inclusion and second projection in the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The projection is a chain map because the shifted differential is $-d_C$. The diagonal cone map $F_b(f)$ makes these sequences into a morphism with other components $f$ and $f[1]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality]. For any integer $n$ they give a commutative five-term diagram with exact rows
$$H^{n-1}(C[1])\to H^n(C)\to H^n(F_b(C))\to H^n(C[1])\to H^{n+1}(C),$$
and the corresponding row for $C'$. If $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so is $f[1]$: kernels and images for the differential $-d_C$ are the same as for $d_C$ with indices shifted by one. Hence the first, second, fourth and fifth vertical maps are isomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] the middle map $H^n(F_b(f))$ is an isomorphism. This holds for every $n$, proving that $F_b$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain, including functoriality; Tag 05QB, lemma-five-lemma

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism $f$, naturality from step 2 writes $T_R(f)=\Phi_{C'}^{-1}F_b(f)\Phi_C$ and $T_L(f)=\Psi_{C'}^{-1}F_b(f)\Psi_C$. Step 3 and functoriality of each cohomology functor show that both maps are quasi-isomorphisms: their cohomology maps are composites of three isomorphisms. Thus tensoring with $P_b$ on either side preserves every quasi-isomorphism. This is precisely the two-sided K-flatness definition of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. No regularity of $b$, boundedness of $C$, or exactness of tensoring an arbitrary object is used.

source.place: kFlat_scalarCone, lines 65-76; its two-sided preservation content proved here directly from steps 1-3

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] to the given closed braided monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions. It supplies the derived tensor, its canonical natural comparison $\mu_{C,P_b}:QC\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b\to Q T_R(C)$, and computation by replacing either argument by a K-flat resolution. In the second argument take the identity quasi-isomorphism $P_b\to P_b$, whose source is K-flat by step 4. This computation says exactly that $\mu_{C,P_b}$ is invertible, even when $C$ is unbounded and not K-flat. Compose it with $Q(\Phi_C)$ to obtain $\theta_C:QC\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b\xrightarrow{\sim}QF_b(C)$. Naturality of the comparison and step 2 give
$$\theta_{C'}\circ(Qf\otimes^{\mathbf L}1)=QF_b(f)\circ\theta_C.$$
The composite is therefore the claimed isomorphism with the specified canonical comparison.

source.place: isIso_μ_scalarCone, lines 78-88, tensorScalarConeIso, lines 146-149, and its naturality, lines 151-158

proof.text: By step 3, $QF_b$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms, since the localization $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] sends them to isomorphisms. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to obtain $\overline F_b:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ and a natural isomorphism $\eta:\overline F_b Q\xrightarrow{\sim}QF_b$. Put $H(X)=X\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b$. The natural isomorphism $\eta^{-1}\theta:HQ\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline F_b Q$ from step 5 lifts by clause (2) of the same node to a natural isomorphism $H\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline F_b$. Its components after precomposition with $Q$ are exactly $\eta_C^{-1}\theta_C$, so the resulting descent has the required compatibility with the displayed isomorphisms. This uses the fixed derived-localization universe, with no new indexing category.
